title: Client Stitch QBR synthesis and decision checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, reuse-first QBR agenda + facilitator script designed for mid-sized accounts (ARR $50k–$500k). Focus: synthesize the last quarter into a short narrative, identify 1–3 renewal risks, and leave with explicit decisions and owners.

Intended outcomes (30 minute core):
- Shared synthesis of customer goals and outcomes this quarter (3 slides worth of evidence)
- Clear renewal posture: green / watch / at-risk with one reason each
- 2 prioritized asks from customer and 2 from Redwood with owners and ETA
- Run this in ~45 minutes (30 min core + 15 min buffer / deep-dive)

Attendees (recommended):
- CSM (lead) — runs synthesis and closes decisions
- Customer success manager (AM) — relationship context
- Technical lead (Redwood solutions eng or SE) — for ramp/usage blockers
- Customer product/ops counterpart (1–2)
- Optional: Account exec for renewal conversation if risk >= watch

Pre-reads (send 72–48h before):
- 1-pager: "This quarter in 6 bullets" (CSM)
- Usage highlights screenshot (Console > Billing & Usage) + 3 anomalies called out (SRE or CSM)
- Active rollout plan/PRD link if there is an integration in progress
- Customer success health snapshot (scorecard export)

Agenda (45 minutes total):
1) Kick + Frame the Outcome (3 mins)
- CSM: Quick intro, purpose, desired decisions (renewal posture + top 2 asks)
- Script: "Thanks all — today we want to align on how the quarter went, surface any surprises, and agree the next 60-day plan so we can remove blockers to your launch/usage goals."

2) Customer synthesis (7 mins)
- CSM: 3-minute narrative: what the customer measured vs. hoped for. Use 1 slide with 3 evidence bullets (metrics, adoption milestone, blocker).
- Customer: 2 mins to add corrections / highlight wins.
- Facilitation prompt: "If I summarize your top win and top blocker in one sentence each, is that right?"

3) Data & usage flash (7 mins)
- Technical lead: Surface top 3 usage signals: token consumption trends, tail latency incidents, error spike windows.
- Script cues: "We saw a 28% MoM increase in production tokens; the median tail latency rose from 120ms to 310ms on X dates — here's the proposed immediate mitigation."

4) Open risks and blockers (7 mins)
- CSM facilitates a quick roundtrip: list top 3 risks with impact and likelihood (1–5).
- Use shorthand decision table: Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner | ETA
- Facilitation tip: For each risk ask: "If this stays as is, what happens to your Q4 objective?"

5) Decision & commitments (10 mins)
- State the renewal posture candidate (green/watch/at-risk) and rationale in one sentence.
- Propose 2 Redwood commitments (e.g., SE whiteboard session, extended test credits, performance investigation priority).
- Ask customer for 2 asks.
- Capture decisions in the Decision Log immediately (see template below).

6) Wrap & next steps (5 mins)
- Confirm owners and dates. Confirm follow-up meeting cadence if needed.
- Close with: "We will circulate the one-page summary and decision log within 48 hours."

Decision Log template (copy into meeting notes):
- Decision ID: auto-increment (e.g., D-2025-09-01-01)
- Decision: short sentence
- Reason: 1–2 bullets
- Owner: name (Redwood or Customer)
- Due date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Status: open / in_progress / closed

Example entry:
- D-2025-09-01-01 | Move to "watch" (renewal) because usage plateaued and integration delays | Impact: potential 10% ARR drag | Owner: Owen Brooks | Due: 2025-09-22 | Status: open

Facilitation script: quick prompts and safety rails
- Opening: "Our goal is alignment on outcomes + at most three tickets to land in the next 60 days. If anything needs deeper time, we schedule a follow-up deep-dive."
- If conversation stalls: "Let's park this in the decision log and agree a 30-minute follow-up with the relevant folks."
- If customer raises a new product ask: "Thank you — can you summarize the ask in 2 bullets and the business outcome? We'll mark it as a product request and prioritize with you."
- For sensitive renewal language: "We'd like to surface the renewal posture candidly so we can act together to remove blockers. Our ask is: are you comfortable with 'watch' as a description right now?"

Renewal risk quick scoring (one-line guidance):
- Green: usage trending up, no active blockers, product unlocking value (score <= 3)
- Watch: stagnating usage, 1 major blocker, or support escalations (score 4–7)
- At-risk: falling usage, executive disengagement, or unresolved integration failure (score >= 8)

Meeting prep checklist (CSM):
- [ ] Draft 1-page synthesis (get signoff from SE if there are technical assertions)
- [ ] Export usage dashboard snapshot and highlight anomalies
- [ ] Confirm attendee list and roles; ping AE if renewal risk is watch+
- [ ] Pre-fill decision log with likely topics to speed capture
- [ ] Prepare one proposed Redwood commitment and 1 potential concession (credits/priority investigations)
- [ ] Schedule follow-up block in calendar tentatively (30–60m)

Meeting prep checklist (SE / Tech):
- [ ] Produce 2–3 datapoints: avg tokens/day, 95th latency, error rate by endpoint
- [ ] Identify top-2 configuration/infra fixes that could materially improve latency/cost
- [ ] Have short troubleshooting playbook ready for on-call referencing

Artifacts to attach to the doc (links to paste into meeting invite):
- Usage snapshot (Console exports)
- Health scorecard (CSV export)
- Open support tickets list (ServiceNow/Jira)
- Active rollout PRD link

Quick renewal tracker (to paste into kickoff sheet or Notion):
- customer: [Company X]
- current ARR: [$120,000]
- renewal date: 2026-01-15
- current posture: watch
- top risk: integration SLA causing delayed rollout
- next milestone: SE deep-dive 2025-09-22
- mitigation owner: Priya Nandakumar

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider trialing a 30-minute "synthesis-only" cadence for low-risk accounts (faster, requires stronger pre-read)
- Could add a single visual: 3-box slide (Wins | Metrics | Blockers) that CSM uses every time — improves consistency
- Keep language simple; customers react better to explicit asks not corporate-speak
- Template should be exportable to Notion and also to the shared QBR folder for audit

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing template):
- Do we want AE to be auto-invited for all watch+ accounts or only on request? (ops decision)
- Should Decision IDs be global or per-account? (global makes cross-account trends easier)

Timestamps / revision log (short):
- 2025-09-12: initial draft (Evan Morales)
- 2025-09-18: added scoring guidance and checklists (Marisol Vega)
- 2025-10-02: incorporated tech datapoint section and linked artifacts (Priya N.)

End of doc — keep this file as the canonical lightweight synthesis template.

(Other riffed phrasing: "stitch" = combine product telemetry + commercial context into a single narrative)
